title: The durable loop
body: Plan, call, observe, repeat — with a checkpoint written after every step. Long runs survive deploys, restarts, and the tool that goes down for twenty minutes.
pointThree: Resume days later from the same state
pointFour: Cancel and rewind to any step
sample: run.resume('8f21c')  # picks up at step 3, not step 0

title: Typed tools
body: Write an ordinary function. Pilot reads its signature, derives the JSON schema, and validates every call before your code runs — so a hallucinated argument is a caught error, not a production incident.

title: State that outlives the process
body: Working memory, scratchpads, and intermediate results live in your database, not in a variable. Nothing is lost to a restart, and two workers never disagree about where a run got to.
pointOne: Postgres, SQLite, or your own driver

title: Human review, anywhere
body: Some decisions should not be automatic. Drop an approval gate into the loop and the run parks itself, routes to the right person, and continues the moment they sign off.
pointTwo: Routing to Slack, email, or your own UI
pointFour: Every approval recorded in the trace

title: Traces you can replay
body: Every prompt, argument, result, token, and cent is recorded per step. Replay a run against a different model or a changed prompt and diff the two side by side before you ship the change.
pointTwo: Replay against a new model or prompt
pointThree: Diff two runs step by step

title: Evals in your pipeline
body: Promote any recorded run to a test case. Your suite runs on every pull request and tells you which step regressed, not just that the score moved.
pointTwo: Assertions per step, not per run

title: Metered spend
body: Cost is attributed to the step that caused it, so you find the expensive loop instead of guessing. Set a ceiling and a run halts rather than quietly billing you for an afternoon.
